title: Meeting minutes
description: What the minutes agent emits: business language, not semantic shapes. It never mints ids or IRIs (those are functions of content), never names a vocabulary type (filing an item under decisions IS the type assignment), and never sees or emits a directory address (the gateway pseudonymises them, and the mapping is the human's).

summary.description: A few sentences a person who missed the meeting could read instead of the transcript.

concepts.description: What the meeting was ABOUT — the systems, capabilities, policies and terms of art discussed. This is the centre of the model: every decision and action must concern at least one.

id.description: Local to THIS document (c1, c2…), never a global id.

label.description: The concept as the speakers named it.

definition.description: What it means, in the speakers' own terms, when they said.

statement.description: The choice that was settled, as one sentence.

rationale.description: Why, if it was said. Never inferred.

concerns.description: Local concept ids this decision is about. At least one — a decision about nothing is not a decision.

decided_by.description: Speaker labels (SPEAKER_00) who settled it. Labels only; who they are is the human's answer, not yours.

resolves.description: A local decision id this supersedes.

commitment.description: What one person owes, as one sentence.

owner.description: The speaker label who owes it.

due.description: YYYY-MM-DD if a date was actually said.

implements.description: A local decision id this carries out.

keywords.description: Terms worth indexing that are not full concepts.

evidence.description: Where in the transcript this came from. OFFSETS, never quotes: a verbatim quote in a queryable graph is unredactable free text.
